description: Refusals: `search` (a one-tick command delay) followed by fourteen `exp` typed without waiting, so the lines queue: the 9th waiting line gets `Why don't you slow down for a few seconds?` and the 13th and later `You are typing too quickly - command ignored`; then `w` into a wall in the arena (`There is no exit in that direction!`), `n` at the closed door, `train` outside a training room, `rest` while a monster attacks (accepted: `You are now resting.`; the next blow ends it), the fight that follows, and logoff. (m1 trim: the monster fight steps 25-30 are left out until monsters exist, T-035/T-040)
behaviours: resting in a spawn room while attacked is accepted and broken by the next blow
`There is no exit in that direction!`
type-ahead echo: queued lines are echoed when they run

mask.why: every direction name carries a random capital letter and a backspace, rewritten each slow cycle: `nJ\borth`
HP/mana in the prompt depend on earlier fights and regen

mask.regex: for \d+ damage|You gain \d+ experience|\d+ (?:copper farthings?|silver nobles?|gold crowns?|platinum pieces?|runic coins?)
mask.why: RNG: damage, experience share, coin drops

notes: The card asked for eight commands without waiting; eight instant commands never queue (each runs at once, no delay), so the burst starts with `search` and has fifteen lines.
Commands typed while others wait are echoed and run one per tick; queued `exp` output interleaves with the monster's attacks.
An earlier run of this script started in the wrong room (the healer's) and sent `a healer`: `You are overcome with a feeling of guilt and break off your attack.` That run was discarded.

burst_check.note: MBBSEmu takes one input byte per host-loop pass and runs its timers in every pass, so on a loaded host the burst can still be arriving at the next fast tick, which drains a queued line and changes the warnings of the lines after it. With the burst queued whole, flood control prints 6 warning lines (5 slow down, the 5th with too quickly) before the first queued line runs; fewer before the first queued echo means a tick landed mid-burst. Then the attempt (steps 5-21) is done again after walking out, and only a whole attempt is kept and compared.
burst_check.warnings: ^(?:Why don't you slow down for a few seconds\?|You are typing too quickly - command ignored)$

steps.note: into the Weapons Shop: a move runs on a fast tick (its command delay ends on the fast tick), so the room and its prompt arrive just after a tick, and the burst sent at once has a whole tick to queue before the next one can drain a line, on both sides
flood: a command with a delay, then no waits
the queue runs one line per tick
back to the Village Entrance, so the rest of the script runs from where it did before
